the-big-goose-and-the-little-white-duck.title: The Big Goose and the Little White Duck
the-big-goose-and-the-little-white-duck.summary: A small white duck and a large goose share a farmyard and slowly learn about each other's very different ways. A gentle, funny story for the youngest listeners.
characters: Little White Duck — small, curious farm duck
the-big-goose-and-the-little-white-duck.note: Details drawn from memory, not verified online; illustrator left null.

the-almost-all-white-rabbity-cat.title: The Almost All-White Rabbity Cat
the-almost-all-white-rabbity-cat.summary: A boy and a cat with rabbit-like looks share a quiet, quirky Dutch-American friendship. The tale is warm and funny, centered on the odd affections that bind animals and people.
characters: Rabbity Cat — odd, almost white cat
the-almost-all-white-rabbity-cat.note: Plot summary kept general; verify details and illustrator.

the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.title: The Little Cow and the Turtle
the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.summary: A little cow wanders off the farm and meets a slow, steady turtle. Their unlikely friendship is told with DeJong's gentle humor.
the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.note: Illustrator and details from memory; unverified.

journey-from-peppermint-street.title: Journey from Peppermint Street
journey-from-peppermint-street.summary: Young Siebren lives in a Dutch village and makes a long journey with his grandfather's old friend across the countryside to a faraway town. Along the way he learns about courage and growing up.
characters: Old Uncle Hendrik — kindly, wise traveler
awards: National Book Award for Children's Books 1969
journey-from-peppermint-street.note: Character names uncertain; award year given from memory.

the-singing-hill.title: The Singing Hill
the-singing-hill.summary: A young girl is lured by the idea of a hill that sings and sets out to find it. Her quest reveals something about courage and belonging.
the-singing-hill.note: Plot details uncertain; keep summary general.

along-came-a-dog.title: Along Came a Dog
along-came-a-dog.summary: A lonely stray dog finds a home on a farm and takes it upon himself to protect a small red hen from a hungry hawk. It's a tender story of devotion between unlikely friends.
characters: Little Red Hen — small, tough, wary

far-out-the-long-canal.title: Far Out the Long Canal
far-out-the-long-canal.summary: Moerie, a boy in a Dutch village, longs to learn to skate on the long canal. His determination takes him far from home.

the-wheel-on-the-school.title: The Wheel on the School
the-wheel-on-the-school.summary: The children of Shora, a Dutch fishing village, wonder why storks no longer nest there and set out to bring them back by finding a wagon wheel for a nest. Their whole village joins in.

the-wheel-on-the-school.setting: Shora, a Friesian village in the Netherlands, mid-20th century

hurry-home-candy.title: Hurry Home, Candy
hurry-home-candy.summary: A small dog named Candy is swept away from his family and has to survive on the streets and in strange homes. The story follows his long hope of making his way back.
hurry-home-candy.setting: A city and countryside in mid-20th century America

the-case-of-the-baker-street-irregular.title: The Case of the Baker Street Irregular

the-case-of-the-baker-street-irregular.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-murdered-players.title: The Case of the Murdered Players

the-case-of-the-murdered-players.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-somerville-secret.title: The Case of the Somerville Secret
the-case-of-the-somerville-secret.summary: A young detective untangles a secret hidden in an old house. Clues and close calls move the story along.
the-case-of-the-somerville-secret.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-threatened-king.title: The Case of the Threatened King
the-case-of-the-threatened-king.summary: A royal figure is threatened and Andrew and his friends try to uncover who is behind it. A brisk mystery with historical flavor.
the-case-of-the-threatened-king.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-watching-boy.title: The Case of the Watching Boy
the-case-of-the-watching-boy.summary: A boy who seems to be watching something he should not leads to a puzzling investigation. A young reader mystery.
the-case-of-the-watching-boy.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-frightened-friend.title: The Case of the Frightened Friend
the-case-of-the-frightened-friend.summary: A friend's alarming fear sets a young sleuth on a hunt for the cause. Clues pile up in this children's mystery.
the-case-of-the-frightened-friend.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-indian-curse.title: The Case of the Indian Curse
the-case-of-the-indian-curse.summary: An old curse seems to be at work and a young detective sets out to find the real explanation. A mystery with eerie touches.
the-case-of-the-indian-curse.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

the-case-of-the-vanishing-corpse.title: The Case of the Vanishing Corpse
the-case-of-the-vanishing-corpse.summary: A body disappears and Andrew Tolliver must discover where it went and why. A spooky puzzle for young readers.
the-case-of-the-vanishing-corpse.note: Details from memory; publication year and series membership unverified.

smith-of-wootton-major-farmer-giles-of-h.title: Smith of Wootton Major & Farmer Giles of Ham
smith-of-wootton-major-farmer-giles-of-h.summary: Two shorter fairy tales in one volume. Farmer Giles is a country man who unexpectedly becomes a dragon-taming hero, while Smith of Wootton Major tells of a village smith who visits the land of Faery.
smith-of-wootton-major-farmer-giles-of-h.setting: Rural England of an imagined past

the-hobbit.title: The Hobbit
the-hobbit.summary: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit, is whisked away by a wizard and thirteen dwarves to win back treasure from a dragon. He discovers unexpected courage and cleverness along the way.
characters: Gollum — riddling creature of the dark
awards: New York Herald Tribune Children's Spring Book Festival prize 1938

the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.title: The Lord of the Rings Trilogy
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.summary: Frodo, a hobbit, inherits a ring of terrible power and sets out with friends to destroy it before the Dark Lord regains it. Their journey spans three volumes of danger, friendship and war.
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.note: Title simplified from notebook listing; published 1954-55 in three volumes.

the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-and-the-ho.title: The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit (4-book set)
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-and-the-ho.summary: A four-book set pairing Bilbo's adventure in The Hobbit with Frodo's quest to destroy the One Ring. Together they form the great story of Middle-earth.

the-lord-of-the-rings.title: The Lord of the Rings
the-lord-of-the-rings.summary: Frodo Baggins and a fellowship of friends set out to destroy a powerful ring and save Middle-earth from the Dark Lord. Told in three parts: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers, and The Return of the King.

anastasia-krupnik.title: Anastasia Krupnik
anastasia-krupnik.summary: Ten-year-old Anastasia keeps lists of what she loves and hates, and struggles with a big change: her parents are expecting a baby. Funny and honest about growing up.

anastasia-again.title: Anastasia Again!
anastasia-again.summary: The Krupniks move from Cambridge to the suburbs, and Anastasia hates it at first. She sets out to make the best of her new home.

number-the-stars.title: Number the Stars
number-the-stars.summary: In Nazi-occupied Copenhagen, ten-year-old Annemarie and her family help shelter her Jewish best friend, Ellen. A moving story of ordinary courage.
characters: Ellen Rosen — Annemarie's Jewish best friend

the-giver.title: The Giver
the-giver.summary: Jonas lives in a seemingly perfect community where everything is controlled. When he is chosen to receive its memories, he starts to question everything.
characters: The Giver — old keeper of memories

the-complete-adventures-of-olga-da-polga.title: The Complete Adventures of Olga da Polga
the-complete-adventures-of-olga-da-polga.summary: Olga da Polga is a proud, talkative guinea pig who tells wild stories about her origins. She has a series of funny adventures with her family and her animal friends.
characters: Olga da Polga — vain, funny guinea pig
the-complete-adventures-of-olga-da-polga.setting: A suburban English home, mid-20th century
the-complete-adventures-of-olga-da-polga.note: Omnibus of Olga stories first published from 1971.

a-bear-called-paddington.title: A Bear Called Paddington
a-bear-called-paddington.summary: The Brown family finds a bear from darkest Peru at Paddington Station, and bring him home. His good manners and mishaps lead to funny chaos.

paddington-at-large.title: Paddington at Large
paddington-at-large.summary: Paddington gets into more scrapes, from sightseeing to shopping to a night at the theater. His good intentions keep causing delightful trouble.
characters: Mr. Gruber — kindly antique shop owner

little-house-books-complete-set.title: Little House Books (complete set)
little-house-books-complete-set.summary: A collection of the beloved books following Laura Ingalls from a log cabin in the Big Woods through frontier life on the prairie and into marriage. They are vivid stories of pioneer hardship and family love.

little-house-books.title: Little House Books
little-house-books.summary: The series follows Laura Ingalls as she grows up on the American frontier. Each book brings the hardships and joys of pioneer family life to life.

on-the-way-home.title: On the Way Home
on-the-way-home.summary: Laura's diary of the 1894 wagon journey from South Dakota to Mansfield, Missouri, with her husband Almanzo and daughter Rose. Rose Wilder Lane added a setting-the-scene introduction.
on-the-way-home.note: Subtitle: The Diary of a Trip from South Dakota to Mansfield, Missouri, in 1894.

the-fledgling.title: The Fledgling
the-fledgling.summary: Georgie Hall longs to fly and befriends a wild Canada goose who teaches her. Her dream captures the village of Concord.

her-majesty-grace-jones.title: Her Majesty, Grace Jones
her-majesty-grace-jones.summary: Grace Jones is a young girl whose imagination can make anything seem possible. Funny and a little odd, this is Langton's first children's book.

the-swing-in-the-summerhouse.title: The Swing in the Summerhouse
the-swing-in-the-summerhouse.summary: A swing in the old summerhouse behind the Hall family's house carries the children into magical, surprising places.
the-swing-in-the-summerhouse.note: Characters and plot from memory; verify.

strawberry-girl.title: Strawberry Girl
strawberry-girl.summary: Birdie Boyer's family moves to rural Florida to grow strawberries, but their rough neighbors, the Slaters, make trouble. A lively portrait of Florida cracker life.

to-be-a-logger.title: To Be a Logger
to-be-a-logger.summary: A boy grows up in the Pacific Northwest and learns the craft and community of logging. Part of Lenski's Roundabout America series.

amos-fortune-free-man.title: Amos Fortune, Free Man
amos-fortune-free-man.summary: Born an African prince, Amos Fortune is captured and enslaved in Massachusetts, and eventually buys his freedom. He settles in New Hampshire and helps others to freedom.

sarah-whitcher-s-story.title: Sarah Whitcher's Story
sarah-whitcher-s-story.summary: Young Sarah Whitcher gets lost in the New Hampshire woods in 1783 and is guarded by a bear. Based on a true local tale.

away-goes-sally.title: Away Goes Sally
away-goes-sally.summary: Sally and her family travel by a house on runners from Massachusetts to Maine in 1800s. Gentle first book of a series.

the-cat-who-went-to-heaven.title: The Cat Who Went to Heaven
the-cat-who-went-to-heaven.summary: A poor Japanese artist is given a little cat who brings luck. He paints a legend of the Buddha, and the cat shows how love changes the world.

the-three-musketeers-adapted-by-carolyn-.title: The Three Musketeers (adapted by Carolyn Sherwin Bailey)
the-three-musketeers-adapted-by-carolyn-.summary: Young d'Artagnan travels to Paris to become a King's Musketeer and befriends Athos, Porthos and Aramis. Together they fight to defend the queen's honor against Cardinal Richelieu's schemes.

the-three-musketeers-complete.title: The Three Musketeers (complete)
the-three-musketeers-complete.summary: D'Artagnan, a young man from Gascony, goes to Paris to join the king's Musketeers and forms an unbreakable friendship with Athos, Porthos and Aramis. They are drawn into court intrigue involving the queen's jewels and the cunning Milady de Winter.

a-trick-of-light.title: A Trick of Light
a-trick-of-light.summary: A girl copes with a family move and puzzling events. A young reader mystery with an emotional core.
a-trick-of-light.note: Plot from memory; unverified, keep summary vague.

the-long-journey.title: The Long Journey
the-long-journey.summary: A young girl sets out on a journey, learning about herself and her family. Corcoran's tale of resilience.

the-girl-with-the-silver-eyes.title: The Girl with the Silver Eyes
the-girl-with-the-silver-eyes.summary: Katie, a girl with silvery eyes, has unusual powers that make her odd to others. Her new friend helps her figure out who she is and find others like her.
the-girl-with-the-silver-eyes.note: Details from memory; verify plot and award.

the-pet-sitting-peril.title: The Pet-Sitting Peril
the-pet-sitting-peril.summary: A pet-sitting job turns frightening when sinister things start to happen. A suspenseful tale for young detectives.

the-haunting.title: The Haunting
the-haunting.summary: Barney is haunted by a ghostly figure who seems to be his late relative. His family's secrets slowly emerge, and he must survive the mystery.

the-blood-and-thunder-adventure-on-hurri.title: The Blood-and-Thunder Adventure on Hurricane Peak
the-blood-and-thunder-adventure-on-hurri.summary: A group of friends takes a wild, madcap trip up a mountain. A lighthearted comic adventure.

catherine-called-birdy.title: Catherine, Called Birdy
catherine-called-birdy.summary: Fourteen-year-old Catherine, nicknamed Birdy, keeps a diary in 1290s England while dodging unwanted suitors arranged by her father. Funny, sharp and surprisingly modern.

the-midwife-s-apprentice.title: The Midwife's Apprentice
the-midwife-s-apprentice.summary: A homeless girl called Brat is taken in by a sharp-tongued midwife. Slowly she gets a name, a home and a purpose.

harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.summary: Orphan Harry Potter learns on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard and is whisked away to Hogwarts School. He finds friends and a mystery involving a hidden stone.
awards: British Book Award 1997 (Children's Book of the Year)
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.note: US title; UK title is Philosopher's Stone.

harry-potter-series.title: Harry Potter series
harry-potter-series.summary: Seven books follow Harry Potter through seven years at Hogwarts as he confronts the dark wizard Voldemort. A story of friendship, courage and growing up.

mary-poppins.title: Mary Poppins
mary-poppins.summary: The magical, stern Mary Poppins arrives on the East Wind to be nanny to the Banks children and takes them on extraordinary outings. She flatly denies it all.

tales-told-near-a-crocodile.title: Tales Told Near a Crocodile
tales-told-near-a-crocodile.summary: Stories collected from Africa, told as storytellers might tell them near a river. A group of traditional tales.

the-summer-birds.title: The Summer Birds
the-summer-birds.summary: Charlotte and her sister meet a strange boy who teaches the children of a village to fly like birds. A haunting first novel.

cat-walk.title: Cat Walk
cat-walk.summary: A stray cat has to survive and make a home. A quiet cat story told with Stolz's gentle touch.

hitty-her-first-hundred-years.title: Hitty, Her First Hundred Years
hitty-her-first-hundred-years.summary: Hitty is a small wooden doll who narrates her hundred years of travels from Maine to the South Seas and India. She sees history through a doll's eyes.

adam-of-the-road.title: Adam of the Road
adam-of-the-road.summary: Adam, an eleven-year-old minstrel's son, is separated from his father and dog in 13th-century England and searches the roads to find them.

the-magic-stone.title: The Magic Stone
the-magic-stone.summary: A magical stone changes the lives of a group of children. A translated Dutch fantasy.
the-magic-stone.note: Could not verify; Dutch original possibly 'De toverkei' and English edition 1970s. Facts may be wrong.

the-exploits-of-moominpappa.title: The Exploits of Moominpappa
the-exploits-of-moominpappa.summary: Moominpappa writes down his youthful adventures as a foundling, meeting the Hemulen and sailing with the Muddler. A funny memoir in the Moomin series.

robinson-crusoe.title: Robinson Crusoe
robinson-crusoe.summary: A shipwrecked Englishman survives for years alone on a tropical island, building shelter and growing food. He later befriends a man he names Friday.

the-bushbabies.title: The Bushbabies
the-bushbabies.summary: Jackie, a girl in Africa, tries to return her pet bushbaby to the forest where it belongs. She travels hundreds of miles with her servant Tembo.

better-known-as-johnny-appleseed.title: Better Known as Johnny Appleseed
better-known-as-johnny-appleseed.summary: The life of John Chapman, who planted orchards across the early American frontier, told with warmth. He is remembered for his kindness to all living things.

ice-king.title: Ice King
ice-king.summary: A story of a man in the ice trade. Unverified.
ice-king.note: Could not identify; may be a transcription error.

all-the-children-were-sent-away.title: All the Children Were Sent Away
all-the-children-were-sent-away.summary: British children are evacuated from London to Canada during World War II. They adjust to a new life far from home.

the-riddle-of-the-red-whale.title: The Riddle of the Red Whale
the-riddle-of-the-red-whale.summary: A boy and his friends try to solve a mystery connected to a whaling vessel. Adventure on the high seas.

the-witch-s-daughter.title: The Witch's Daughter
the-witch-s-daughter.summary: On a Scottish island, three children meet a mysterious girl called the witch's daughter. They help her through a dangerous adventure.
characters: Tim, Janey, Perdita's friends — curious children

bunnicula-a-rabbit-tale-of-mystery.title: Bunnicula: A Rabbit-Tale of Mystery
bunnicula-a-rabbit-tale-of-mystery.summary: The Monroe family's cat Chester becomes convinced that their new pet rabbit is a vampire. The family dog Harold narrates their funny investigation.

the-ark.title: The Ark
the-ark.summary: A German family displaced after World War II finds a way to rebuild their lives in an old army barracks. A story of hope and cooperation.

the-joke-shop.title: The Joke Shop
the-joke-shop.summary: Children discover a joke shop with unusual powers. Poet Enright's comic children's novel.

the-unicorn-treasury.title: The Unicorn Treasury
the-unicorn-treasury.summary: A collection of stories and poems about unicorns, edited by Bruce Coville. It brings together tales from many writers.

homesick-my-own-story.title: Homesick: My Own Story
homesick-my-own-story.summary: Jean Fritz remembers her childhood in China in the 1920s, longing for a home she had never seen in America. A warm memoir.

robin-hood.title: Robin Hood
robin-hood.summary: The classic legend of the outlaw archer who robs the rich to help the poor in Sherwood Forest. Illustrated by N. C. Wyeth.

watership-down.title: Watership Down
watership-down.summary: A band of rabbits flees their doomed warren and searches for a new home on Watership Down. Along the way they face dangers, rival warrens, and friendship.

witch-s-sister.title: Witch's Sister
witch-s-sister.summary: A girl suspects her sister's friend is a witch and tries to prove it. First in the Witch series.

david-copperfield.title: David Copperfield
david-copperfield.summary: A shortened version of Dickens's tale of orphan David Copperfield. He grows up through hardship, school and work to become a writer.
characters: Mr. Micawber — cheerful, always in debt

unreal-eight-surprising-stories.title: Unreal! Eight Surprising Stories
unreal-eight-surprising-stories.summary: Eight offbeat, funny and slightly gross stories with twist endings. A hit among young Australian readers.

the-dark-thirty-southern-tales-of-the-su.title: The Dark-Thirty: Southern Tales of the Supernatural
the-dark-thirty-southern-tales-of-the-su.summary: Ghost stories drawn from African American tradition, each reflecting history and community. Told at dusk, they are spooky and thought-provoking.

the-little-bookroom.title: The Little Bookroom
the-little-bookroom.summary: A collection of Farjeon's own favourite short stories and fairy tales, with a mix of fantasy and gentle humor.

jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.title: Jimmy, the Pickpocket of the Palace
jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.summary: A retelling of The Frog Prince from the frog's viewpoint. A funny fairy tale with a twist.

my-friends-the-wild-chimpanzees.title: My Friends the Wild Chimpanzees
my-friends-the-wild-chimpanzees.summary: Goodall describes her early years observing chimpanzees at Gombe Stream. A National Geographic book for young readers.
my-friends-the-wild-chimpanzees.note: Original author name Jane van Lawick-Goodall; normalized to Jane Goodall.

yolonda-s-genius.title: Yolonda's Genius
yolonda-s-genius.summary: Yolonda's little brother Andrew is a harmonica genius. As a fifth-grader, she works hard to give him the chance he deserves.

the-poisonwood-bible.title: The Poisonwood Bible
the-poisonwood-bible.summary: An American missionary family moves to the Belgian Congo in 1959. Told by the wife and four daughters, it shows how their lives unravel.
the-poisonwood-bible.note: Adult novel, not a children's book.

Meindert DeJong.bio: Meindert DeJong was born in a small Friesian village and emigrated to the United States as a child. He wrote warm, humane stories for children, often about animals and Dutch village life. He won the Newbery Medal and the Hans Christian Andersen Award.

Robert Newman.bio: Robert Newman was an American author best known for children's mysteries. He wrote detective stories in a series. Few biographical details could be verified.
known_for: The Case of the Baker Street Irregular
The Case of the Vanishing Corpse

J. R. R. Tolkien.bio: J. R. R. Tolkien was a philologist and Oxford professor who created Middle-earth. He began writing The Hobbit as a bedtime story for his children. He fought in World War I and shaped modern fantasy.

Lois Lowry.bio: Lois Lowry grew up in a military family and lived in many places. She is known for writing both humorous and serious children's books. She has won two Newbery Medals.

Michael Bond.bio: Michael Bond worked as a BBC cameraman before creating Paddington. He saw a lonely toy bear on a shelf on Christmas Eve 1956 and was inspired. The books became beloved worldwide.

Laura Ingalls Wilder.bio: Laura Ingalls Wilder grew up on the American frontier and became a teacher. In her sixties she wrote her childhood memories as the Little House books. Her daughter Rose helped edit them.
known_for: Little House in the Big Woods

Jane Langton.bio: Jane Langton wrote fantasies and mysteries set in Concord, Massachusetts. She illustrated some of her own books. She won a Newbery Honor.

Lois Lenski.bio: Lois Lenski was an author and illustrator who wrote regional stories. She visited the places she wrote about to get the details right. She won the Newbery Medal for Strawberry Girl.

Elizabeth Yates.bio: Elizabeth Yates wrote many children's books and biographies. Her work often drew on New England life. She won the Newbery Medal for Amos Fortune, Free Man.

Elizabeth Coatsworth.bio: Elizabeth Coatsworth was a poet and children's author who lived in Maine. She won the Newbery Medal for The Cat Who Went to Heaven. She was married to writer Henry Beston.
known_for: The Cat Who Went to Heaven

Alexandre Dumas.bio: Alexandre Dumas was a prolific French novelist and playwright. His father was a general of mixed-race heritage. His adventure novels remain popular.

Carolyn Sherwin Bailey.bio: Carolyn Sherwin Bailey was an American children's author and educator. She won the Newbery Medal for Miss Hickory. She adapted classics for young readers.

Barbara Corcoran.bio: Barbara Corcoran was a teacher and author of young adult novels. She wrote on teens facing life challenges. She lived in Montana.

Willo Davis Roberts.bio: Willo Davis Roberts wrote suspense and mysteries for young readers and adults. She published over a hundred books. She won several awards.
known_for: The Girl with the Silver Eyes

Margaret Mahy.bio: Margaret Mahy was a New Zealand librarian who became a celebrated children's writer. She won the Carnegie Medal twice and the Hans Christian Andersen Award. She was known for flamboyant costumes.

Karen Cushman.bio: Karen Cushman was inspired by her studies of medieval history. She wrote historical fiction about girls. She won the Newbery Medal for The Midwife's Apprentice.

J. K. Rowling.bio: J. K. Rowling conceived the idea for Harry Potter on a delayed train. She wrote the first book as a single mother. The series became the best-selling book series in history.
known_for: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

P. L. Travers.bio: P. L. Travers was born Helen Lyndon Goff and worked as a dancer and actress. She created Mary Poppins while living in England. She had a rocky relationship with Disney's film.

Humphrey Harman.bio: Humphrey Harman wrote on Africa and told African tales. Little verified biographical information is available.

Penelope Farmer.bio: Penelope Farmer is an English author known for children's fantasy. Her novels, including Charlotte Sometimes, are known for being thoughtful.

Mary Stolz.bio: Mary Stolz wrote more than 60 books for children and teens. She was a Newbery Honor recipient.

Rachel Field.bio: Rachel Field was a poet, novelist and playwright. She won the Newbery Medal for Hitty. She died young at age 47.

Elizabeth Janet Gray.bio: Elizabeth Janet Gray, later Vining, was a children's author who won the Newbery Medal for Adam of the Road. She later became tutor to Crown Prince Akihito of Japan.

Leonie Kooiker.bio: Leonie Kooiker is a Dutch children's author. Little verified information is available.

Tove Jansson.bio: Tove Jansson was a Finnish-Swedish artist and writer who created the Moomins. She won the Hans Christian Andersen Medal in 1966. She spent summers on a tiny island.

Daniel Defoe.bio: Daniel Defoe was a merchant, journalist and novelist. He wrote Robinson Crusoe near the end of his life. He is often called a father of the English novel.

William Stevenson.bio: William Stevenson was a Canadian journalist and author. He wrote A Man Called Intrepid and The Bushbabies.

Mabel Leigh Hunt.bio: Mabel Leigh Hunt was an American children's author with Quaker roots. She wrote historical fiction. She won a Newbery Honor for Better Known as Johnny Appleseed.

Sheila Garrigue.bio: Sheila Garrigue is an American author who wrote about children's lives during the war. She was inspired by true evacuee stories.
known_for: All the Children Were Sent Away
The Eternal Spring of Mr. Ito

Edward Fenton.bio: Edward Fenton was an American writer and translator. He wrote adventure novels for young readers.
known_for: The Riddle of the Red Whale

Nina Bawden.bio: Nina Bawden wrote both novels for adults and children. She was evacuated during WWII, an experience that shaped her fiction. She was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

Deborah Howe.bio: Deborah Howe was an American author who co-wrote Bunnicula with her husband James. She died young.

James Howe.bio: James Howe is an American author who wrote the Bunnicula series. His books range from humor to serious issues.

Margot Benary-Isbert.bio: Margot Benary-Isbert was a German-American author who emigrated after World War II. She wrote about postwar family life in Germany.

D. J. Enright.bio: D. J. Enright was a poet, novelist and critic who taught in several countries. He wrote a few books for children.

Bruce Coville.bio: Bruce Coville has written many fantasy books for children. He worked as a toymaker and a teacher.

Jean Fritz.bio: Jean Fritz was born in China to missionary parents and moved to the US as a teen. She wrote lively, well-researched histories and biographies for children.
known_for: And Then What Happened, Paul Revere?

Paul Creswick.bio: Paul Creswick was an English author known for his retelling of Robin Hood, later illustrated by N. C. Wyeth. Few biographical details could be verified.

Richard Adams.bio: Richard Adams worked as a civil servant before publishing Watership Down. He first told the story to his daughters on a car journey. It became a huge success.

Phyllis Reynolds Naylor.bio: Phyllis Reynolds Naylor wrote over 140 books. She won the Newbery Medal for Shiloh. She started writing as a child.

Charles Dickens.bio: Charles Dickens worked in a factory as a child while his father was in debtors' prison. He became the most popular novelist of his day. His characters are among the best known in literature.

Gertrude Moderow.bio: No verified information found about this adaptor.

Paul Jennings.bio: Paul Jennings is an Australian author known for funny, gross and surprising short stories. He grew up in Australia. His stories are popular with reluctant readers.

Patricia C. McKissack.bio: Patricia McKissack wrote many books on African American history and folklore. She and her husband Fredrick wrote together. She won a Newbery Honor.

Eleanor Farjeon.bio: Eleanor Farjeon was an English poet and storyteller who grew up in a literary family. She wrote hymns and fairy tales. The Eleanor Farjeon Award honors her.
known_for: Martin Pippin in the Apple Orchard

Donna Jo Napoli.bio: Donna Jo Napoli is a linguistics professor and children's writer. She retells fairy tales with fresh angles.
known_for: Jimmy, the Pickpocket of the Palace

Jane Goodall.bio: Jane Goodall was a primatologist who studied wild chimpanzees at Gombe. She started with no formal training. She became a leading conservation advocate.

Carol Fenner.bio: Carol Fenner was a children's author and illustrator. She won a Newbery Honor for Yolonda's Genius.

Barbara Kingsolver.bio: Barbara Kingsolver trained as a biologist and became a novelist. She grew up partly in the Congo. She is known for literary fiction with social themes.
